788
RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for WRITTEN ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Thursday, the May 18, 2006/Vaisakha 28, 1928 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Prime Minister; Atomic Energy; Coal; Communications and
Information Technology; External Affairs; Information and Broadcasting;
Overseas Indian Affairs; Panchayati Raj; Parliamentary Affairs;
Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions; Planning; Shipping,
Road Transport and Highways; Space; Statistics and Programme
Implementation; Urban Development; Urban Employment and
Poverty Alleviation; Youth Affairs and Sports)
Total number of questions —155
Generation from RAPS
3486. SHRI RAMDAS AGARWAL:
SHRI LALIT KISHORE
CHATURVEDI:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Unit-1 of
Rajasthan Atomic Energy Power Station
(RAPS), Rawatbhata has stopped
generation since October, 2004;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) by when it is likely to recommence
the generation;
(d) the steps being taken by
Government to compensate Rajasthan for
loss of generation from RAPS Unit-1;
(e) whether any request have been
received from the State Government of
Rajasthan to enhance allocation from RAPS
Unit-III to VI; and
(f) if so, the steps that have been taken
so far by Government to meet the demand
of the State, till date?
Generation of electricity from atomic
power in Rajasthan
†3487. SHRI LALIT KISHORE
CHATURVEDI: Will the PRIME
MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether any survey had been
conducted to generate electricity from
atomic power at any other place also in
addition to Rawatbhata in Rajasthan;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether based on the said survey
the possibility of establishing an atomic
power station on the bank of Mahi Bajaj
Sagar in Bansbara district had been
expressed;
(d) if so, the details of the progress made
in this regard so far; and

(e) whether in order to explore the
possibilities of installing an atomic power
station elsewhere also in Rajasthan, the
proposal to conduct surveys is under
consideration?
Advantages for joining ITER
3488. SHRIMATI S.G. INDIRA: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that India would
join ITER in a few days;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the advantages in case India joins
the ITER; and
(d) what are the other nations who have
already joined the ITER?
Uranium Project in Nalagonda (A.P.)
3489. SHRI JESUDASU SEELAM:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
have accorded environmental clearance to
the uranium project proposed to be set-up
in Nalagonda District and two other places;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the precautions that have been taken
regarding (i) endanger people’s health, and
(ii) olegraoation of environment; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Supply of Uranium to Heavy Water
Reactors
3490. SHRI EKANATH K. THAKUR:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that India's nuclear
power programme is heading for a crisis as
natural uranium, the fuel that drives 13
Pressurized Heavy Water Reactors
(PHWRS) in the country, is in short
supply;
(b) whether it is a fact that the load
factor achieved by the nuclear power
stations has come down due to non-
availability of nuclear fuel as the
development of domestic mines has not
kept pace with addition of generating
capacity; and
(c) if so, the steps Government propose
to take so as to provide enough supply of
natural uranium for 13 PHWRS in the
country?
Import, demand and production of coal
3491. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT:
Will the Minister of COAL be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
are planning to import coal;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the estimated coal reserves in the
country;
(d) annual demand and production of
coal in the country; and
(e) the reasons for Government not
being able to produce sufficient quantity
of coal from its own mines to meet the
domestic requirement?
Pneumoconiosis cases in coal mines
3492. SHRI MOINUL HASSAN
AHAMED: Will the Minister of COAL
be pleased to state:
(a) the total number of cases of
pneumoconiosis detected in coal mines in
all the subsidiary of Coal India Ltd. and
captive coal mines given to private
companies during the last three years;

(b) the steps taken by the coal
companies to give them adequate treatment
and package of rehabilitation;
(c) the measures being taken by the coal
companies to prevent recurrence of
Pneumoconiosis; and
(d) the role of Government in this
regard?

chalk out emergency measures to step up
